docs.bodySnippet: [Transcript of the meeting video — Finance Committee 09-18-23] Context/Agenda: # Finance Committee 09-18-23 Context/Agenda: welcome everybody to the September 18th 2023 Finance Committee meeting um thanks for everybody for being here today please turn your cell phones to either mute or vibrate um we only have a few items on the agenda today Dr. Aldrich is joining us on Zoom and um before we get started on the agenda just like to say our city clerk Chris Jones is having a big birthday tomorrow so I'd hope like to wish you a happy birthday thank you for everything you do for us and for the city and I hope everybody had a better weekend than my Broncos which wouldn't take much uh with that we'll start off with the first item on the agenda please number 20 resolution reappropriating the fiscal year 2024 budget of the city of Cheyenne according to the provisions of Wyoming state statute 16-4-112 and 16-4-113 staff report uh good afternoon Robin Lockman City Treasurer uh before you is the first reappropriation of fiscal year 2024. in addition to the encumbrances carryover balances and new grants that I discussed in my memo there are six general fund Reserve requests I'd like to quickly cover the first request is for 720 for the City Council budget to pay for a city issued cell phone for a member of City Council the second request is for janitorial and HVAC contract increases in the amount of twenty two thousand two or three hundred and twenty seven dollars that were approved by the governing body on June 26th these contracts cover various City facilities the third request is just a reclassification of how we previously accounted for investment advisor fees previously the fees were just paid through an offset to investment Revenue for better transparency I decided to separate these costs and include them as an expense of the city rather than in a revenue offset fourth request is for 107 115 which is the balance remaining in a contract with Davis and Canon LLP for Real Property litigation representation for Thomas Heights Stephanie boster is here in case you have questions on this contractor request the fifth request is from community recreation and events director Jason Sanchez to transfer additional funds into both the Civic Center and the ice and Event Center funds in the amount of 469 270 as I indicated in my memo the cre department and the general fund turned back 714 884 in unspent funds as of June 30th of 2023. Jason is in attendance if you have questions on this request finally the mayor has requested ninety five thousand five hundred and fifty dollars to pay for ground operations and crane expenses related to moving rail cars donated by the Union Pacific Railroad for the 15th Street Rail Project I believe the mayor and Tom are here if you have questions on this request there is one other non-general fund request that I'd like to highlight in the amount of seven hundred fifty thousand dollars this is in the bailboard recreation fund and will be used to pay for trail designs roadway access construction and parking area and restrooms this request will be paid for by reserves in this fund that were accumulated from the wind energy lease payments

is the newest ordinance defining the terms and conditions for officers for fiscal year 23-24. this is something we redo every year the only change in here is the minimum numbers of hours overtime for court call outs it was one hour the employee Association requested we change it to two I did some research on it and very few of the Court overtime inputs in our system were less than two hours anyway so it'll have very little fiscal impact on the police department and I stand for any questions thank you Captain James any questions from committee yes sir Dr. Aldrich chairman white through you um Kevin James can you just and Paige Exhibit C page one it talks about specialty call pay plan schedule and I'm I was just curious as I was reading through this if you can tell us how many of each of cumulative amount um I cannot tell you how many for each but I can get that together and get it sent to you and we do have a few but not very many most the ones that are multiples are the field training officers so they're a field training officer and they're a canine Handler or um you know they wouldn't be field training and detectives because detective does not do field training but we do have a few but they're most likely to say mostly the field training officers will carry two okay yeah if you could number I'm just curious um if you know people are if that's really they're taking it to invite Elizabeth stump our chairperson up to the podium to give the state of the youth address hello my name is Elizabeth stump and I am the chair of the Cheyenne mayor's youth Council I've been a member of the youth Council for the past four years first off I would like to thank the sponsor of mayor's youth Council Devin pies for all of her guidance and contributions to the council secondly I'd like to thank Stacy Becker for all of her efforts both of them have helped to make this year go incredibly well also I am grateful for the council's executive team Kristen and Maddie Huffman for every one of you better we first started off our year with team building activities including a ropes course then we organized a holiday Extravaganza activity for families at the Cheyenne Children's Village next we got to see the water treatment plant along with the public safety building on a day off from school we ended the year with volunteering at the youth day of giving event and with our docs.bodySnippet: [Transcript of the meeting video — Finance Committee 04-03-23] Context/Agenda: # Finance Committee 04-03-23 Context/Agenda: I think welcome everybody to the April 3rd 2023 Finance Committee meeting all committee members are present for those who will be making any type of public comment please approach the podium and identify yourself when that time comes also if you could please make sure that your cell phones are on vibrate or mute we will we won't be discussing any other items than those interested on the agenda and with that uh Jen if you could please read the first item number 15 resolution providing for the adoption of a fund balance policy in accordance with the governmental accounting standard board gasby statement number 54. staff report hi good afternoon Robin Lockman City Treasurer before you is a proposed policy that addresses the level of unrestricted fund balance commonly referred to as reserves that should be maintained in the city's general fund her resolution 5605 which was adopted back in 2014. the city is required to maintain a minimum of 60 days of general fund operating Reserves each seven days is of operating reserves equals a little over one million dollars my recommendation is to increase this level to a minimum of 120 days this policy outlines the recommendation as well as what needs to occur if this level ever drops below that 120 days due to an economic downturn or an expense an unanticipated expenditures the city as of the end of February has 224 days of operating reserves this equates to nearly 37.7 million dollars of that amount 27.6 million is considered spendable for the current policy of 60 days if the 120 day policy is approved the current spendable amount will be lowered to 17.5 million the policy also addresses how funds are committed and assigned under this policy and current practice the mayor is authorized to assign reserves for specific purposes which is much less restrictive than committing reserves which is only the governing body can do a recent example of an assignment by mayor Collins is the two million dollars that he assigned back in 2021 to help pay 59 of the fire pension a liability that the city currently has which is about 4.9 million examples of commitments that the governing body does are when I um ask you for a reappropriation or the budget ordinance that takes Reserves um the governing body can override an assignment by the mayor as well um also for comparison in the memo that I wrote to you I provided um the different municipalities in Wyoming and their docs.bodySnippet: [Transcript of the meeting video — 01-27-23 KLWY-FOX 27 Mayor Collins Interview] Context/Agenda: # 01-27-23 KLWY-FOX 27 Mayor Collins Interview Context/Agenda: you know I think the the first bill that we're really passionate about is Senate file 13. that's the one that gives us more Bar and Grill licenses if you think about Cheyenne Olive Garden Wasabi Grill uh Guadalajara uh Napoli's those all have Bar and Grill licenses and we're out of those and so if another restaurant wants to come we're we're limited in our ability to help them with the liquor license uh to be able to do that so this bill gives us more seven more of those uh those liquor licenses and then it also expands it by by coming up with a uh an addition to not only being a restaurant bill but we also have our ability to use entertainment so let's look at a bowling alley or something like that now we would be able to help them with the same license so 60 of your revenues have to come from food and or entertainment and so we're really passionate about that bill we've worked all summer as we've talked about before on getting this bill passed and we think it's a good bill so uh Wham is the Wyoming Association of municipalities and it's our our association for cities and towns Mayors City Council people and they're here in town this week I find it really inspiring to be around other folks you
